Two kinds of inconsistency would break code that calls the registry generically. I didn't edit any files. There are no callers of the registry outside `shop/carriers/`, so I checked the modules against each other, not against real usage.

## 1. `maple.py` takes weight in grams; the other 19 take kilograms

`shop/carriers/maple.py:2-25` documents "weight in grams" and uses `PER_GRAMS = 3` and `MAX_GRAMS = 30000`. Every other carrier takes kilograms and caps at 30–49.

The method signature is the same as everywhere else (`rate(self, weight: float, zone="local")`), so nothing fails. A caller passing kilograms gets a wrong price with no error:

- `get("maple").rate(5)` returns 509 cents (494 + 3×5). The per-kg carriers charge around 2,000 cents for 5 kg.
- Weights up to 30,000 are accepted, so a kilogram value never trips the range check.

This is the most serious problem because it gives no sign that anything is wrong. Checkout would show a much lower price for maple.

## 2. Four carriers have no `tracking_url`

These modules define `rate`, `label` and `valid_label` but not `tracking_url`:

- `shop/carriers/delta.py`
- `shop/carriers/kestrel.py`
- `shop/carriers/onyx.py`
- `shop/carriers/tundra.py`

Any call like `get(name).tracking_url(code)` raises `AttributeError` for these four carriers.

## Checked and consistent

- All 20 classes expose `name`, which matches their registry key.
- `rate` has the same signature everywhere, returns an `int` in cents, and raises `ValueError` when weight is out of range.
- Every `ZONES` table has the same keys: `local`, `regional` and `national`.
- `label` and `valid_label` use the same `PREFIX-%08d` format in every module, and each one accepts the labels it produces.
